2. In the writ petition, the petitioners state that the land measuring an area of 64.5 acres appertaining to C.S. Plots No.79, 80 and 82 under Mouza Dhaka City, Sheet No.38, Word No.2 corresponding to SA Plot No.3505, 3573 and 3512 under SA Khatian No.1960 and 1964 respectively (the schedule property) belonged to late Meer Md. Nawab Ali. After his death Meer Md. Khizir Ali as son inherited the property. After death of Meer Md. Khizri All the petitioners and four others became the owners of the schedule property by inheritance. The schedule property was acquired by the respondents under LA Case No.2 of 1997-98 for construction of flood control embankment under taken by the Water Development Board. Out of nine co-shares, four co-heirs were given their proportionate compensation showing the schedule property as viti land leaving the five petitioners although the property was ejmaly property. The petitioners produced all papers in support of their title and possession as per requirement of the respondents. Despite the respondents refrained themselves from making the payment in favour of the petitioners. 

 5. It is further stated in the affidavit-in-opposition that S.A. plot No.3505 had not been acquired and that compensation was taken for the area of 0.0645, 0.0604, 0.0323, 0.0062 acres under S.A. plots No.3512 and 3573 of Mouza Shahar, Dhaka including the case land. Subsequently, form the official record and the khatians the schedule property was foimd as diluvium land and thereby the Government being the owner of the same payment of compensation was stopped on 10.09.2002 and that the respondents also took steps for realization of disbursed money in accordance with section 16 of the Ordinance, 1982. 

 6. Mr. Abdus Slam Khan, the learned Advocate with Mr. Humayun Kabir Sikder, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the owners of the acquired land as per the record of right and that considering title and possession, some of the co-shares were paid compensation to their proportionate shares but with malafide intention and ulterior motives the respondents are refrained themselves from paying compensation to the petitioners inspite of repeated approaches to them. He further submits that S.A. Khatian reflects the name of the petitioners' predecessor and that pursuant to same the petitioners got their names in the R.S. Khatian and paid all the taxes for the schedule property. Inspite of the facts, the respondents are not paying them compensation as heirs of S.A. recorded owners. He also submits that the schedule property are the viti land but denying the fact, the respondents are not paying compensation on the plea that the land are now under water (shikosti land). He again submits that previously parts of the plots in question were acquired in connection with another project under LA Case No.8 of 1993-94 and that the petitioners were allowed to receive compensation for the said acquisition. Therefore, in the present LA Case the respondents cannot deny the payment in respect of same nature of land. Referring to the case of Abdul Latif Howlader vs. Bangladesh Power Development Board and others reported in 46 DLR page 384, Mr. Khan lastly submits that under the writ jurisdiction this Court has the authority to adjudicate the matter of civil nature and therefore, entitlement of petitioners to receive compensation under LA proceeding can be determined under this writ jurisdiction. 

 7. In contrast, Mr. Md. Yonus Ali, the learned Assistant Attorney General (AAG) appearing for the respondent No.3 contends that the record of right i.e. S.A. khatian describes the schedule property as shikosti land and therefore it being vested with the Government as per law the petitioners are not entitled to have any compensation for the Shikosti land. To substantiate the submission the learned A.A.G. refers to the case of Human Rights and Peace for Bangladesh and others Vs. Bangladesh & others reported in 14 BLC page 759. He further contends that some of the co-heirs having been paid compensation, the respondents have already issued notice under Section 16 of the Ordinance, 1982 and the process for refunding of the same are now pending and therefore, the petitioners cannot claim compensation on the plea of receipt of compensation by those co-heirs. He again contents that the relevant Khatians show the property as shikosti land i.e. land under water and thereby the petitioners claim as to viti land is a disputed question of fact which cannot be decided under writ jurisdiction. The learned A.A.G. vehemently raised the question of maintainability of the writ petition on the ground that Section 28 of the Ordinance, 1982 provides remedy for settling dispute regarding payment of compensation under acquisition process and that without availing the same, the petitioners cannot maintain the present writ petition. 

 9. In support of title and possession the petitioners annexed the SA Khatians regarding the schedule property (Annexures A/2 and A/3 to the writ petition). Although those khatians were recorded in the name of petitioners' predecessor but nature of the schedule property has been mentioned as "SHIKOSHTI BHUMI". The Government developed the said shikosti land and constructed flood control embankment. This being the position according the record of right question arise who is entitled to the said property in view of Section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (the Act, 1950).
